keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 23,424 km2 (bbox 40.1-42.9E, 41.3-43.5N) lies on Colchis, from the Chorokhi mouth to the Abkhaz coast. The page gives no area and no boundary (it names Archaeopolis, Phasis, and the neighbouring Abasgians), and nothing dated for 638; the shape is accepted at the honest precision of the era. The page has the kingdom 'incorporated into the Byzantine Empire as a province' by the end of the 7th century.

23,545 km2 (+0.5 percent): redrawing noise at the moment the Rashidun shape touches it. The Arab-Khazar wars page: after the 640s-650s Arab settlement 'only Lazica (on the Black Sea coast) remained under Byzantine influence'; no change of Lazic land is dated.
23,424 km2 (-0.5 percent): noise; the page has no event in 682 (the last Patricius, c. 696/697, comes later).

Neither it nor the Abasgia page (largely silent; only an undated 'Lazian Wars left the Kingdom of Lazica disintegrated') dates a transfer in 724, so the shape is kept as drawn and the ledger event is confidence 1.

777: Leon II of Abasgia takes Lazica by dynastic union. 'Leon II exploited this dynastic union to acquire Lazica in the 770s'; 'Towards circa 778, Leon II won his full independence with the help of the Khazars' and took the title 'King of the Abkhazians'. The year is Cliopatria's last Lazica year; the Lazica page instead ends the kingdom in 697: the last Patricius 'revolted against the Byzantine hegemony and acknowledged the suzerainty of the Arabs' (c. 696/697).

notes:
ONE STATE, TWO ROWS. Cliopatria's Lazica (-63..545) and Kingdom of Lazica (638..777) share the Wikipedia article and Wikidata Q136884. The page treats them as one kingdom (established 131, last king Tzath II in 556, kingdom surviving as a Byzantine dependency to 697 and the Abkhazian union of the 770s). The earlier slug is lazica, which a different batch of eu-19 writes, so this dossier starts in 638 and hands over from lazica; the orchestrator may prefer to merge the two (one dossier under lazica listing both Names) and drop this one. The gap 546-637 is not drawn by Cliopatria except as Georgia 567-576 (the eastern-roman-empire notes call that Lazica) and nobody has verified it.

START AND END. 638 and 777 are Cliopatria's. The page ends the kingdom in 697 (infobox 'Disestablished: 697'; 'incorporated into the Byzantine Empire as a province' by the end of the 7th century; the last Patricius, c. 696/697, 'acknowledged the suzerainty of the Arabs'); the Kingdom of Abkhazia page has Leon II 'acquire Lazica in the 770s'. I kept 777 because the land is drawn in Cliopatria to then and the Abkhazia page treats Lazica as a polity that could be acquired. The suzerain relations (Byzantine patricius to c. 697, Arab acknowledgement after) are vassal_start/end events for the byzantine-empire and umayyad-caliphate dossiers with counterpart kingdom-of-lazica; no page gives an end year for them.

724. The only shape change in the record (-21 percent) has no page: confidence 1. The Georgia row 724-777 is the principality of Abasgia, which the kingdom-of-abkhazia dossier (not yet written) should own.

GAZETTEER. Nothing missing: Colchis resolves. Archaeopolis coordinates are Nokalakevi's (approximate).

BUDGET. Four pages against up to five; the Abasgia page was thin.
